basic_details.job_title: IARI Young Professional II Recruitment 2026 – Walkin
basic_details.short_information: Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) is recruiting candidates for 1 Young Professional-II post on a contractual basis through a walk-in interview on 20 November 2026. Eligible applicants holding a Post Graduate Degree (M. Sc.) in Plant Biochemistry/ Plant Molecular Biology/ Biotechnology/ Plant Physiology/ Environmental Science/ Bioinformatics can attend the walk-in interview in person at the venue given in the official notification. important_instructions: The position is purely temporary and will be filled on a contractual basis, co-terminus with the project. The Global CoE on millets project is currently approved up to 31 March 2027, but is likely to be extended further. No TA/DA or any other expenses will be paid for attending the interview. Only candidates having essential qualifications would be entertained for the interview. Selected candidates shall not claim for regular appointments at the Institute as the post is co-terminus with the project. Concealing of facts or canvassing in any form shall lead to disqualification or termination. Candidates whose near or distant relatives are employees of ICAR/IARI must declare their name, designation, nature of duties, and relationship in writing. If a relative is found to be an employee of ICAR/IARI on the date of the interview, the candidate will not be allowed to appear. In case of any discrepancy, the English version shall be treated as final. The Institute retains the right not to select any candidate or scrap any of the positions even after the interview.

content_sections.heading: IARI Young Professional-II Job Description
content_sections.text: The selected Young Professional-II will work on the project entitled “Omics-based Interventions for Characterizing the Pearl Millet Genotypes for Rancidity and Development of Nutri-Rich Processed Products with Improved Bioavailability, and Shelf-Life” (GCoE on Millets 12-258 TG3361) under the Division of Biochemistry, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi 110012. content_sections.heading: What to Bring
content_sections.text: Two copies of the application form as per the format given in Annexure 1. A copy of biodata with duly attested certificates of 10th, 12th, under-graduation, post-graduation, Ph.D., and other certificates. An attested recent passport size photograph affixed on the bio-data. All original documents and medical certificate at the time of joining (if selected). No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the current employer, if working.

content_sections.heading: What Happens on the Day
content_sections.text: Candidates having essential qualifications will be entertained for the walk-in interview in person on 20 November 2026. Selected candidates will be required to produce all original documents and a medical certificate at the time of joining.

content_sections.heading: IARI Young Professional-II Important Instructions
content_sections.text: The position is purely temporary and will be filled on a contractual basis, co-terminus with the project. The Global CoE on millets project is currently approved up to 31 March 2027, but is likely to be extended further. No TA/DA or any other expenses will be paid for attending the interview. Only candidates having essential qualifications would be entertained for the interview. Selected candidates shall not claim for regular appointments at the Institute as the post is co-terminus with the project. Concealing of facts or canvassing in any form shall lead to disqualification or termination. Candidates whose near or distant relatives are employees of ICAR/IARI must declare their name, designation, nature of duties, and relationship in writing. If a relative is found to be an employee of ICAR/IARI on the date of the interview, the candidate will not be allowed to appear. In case of any discrepancy, the English version shall be treated as final. The Institute retains the right not to select any candidate or scrap any of the positions even after the interview.

faq.question: Q1. When is the IARI Young Professional-II walk-in interview?
faq.answer: The walk-in interview will be held on 20 November 2026.

faq.question: Q2. Where is the walk-in interview venue?
faq.answer: The interview will take place at the Division of Biochemistry, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi 110012.

faq.question: Q3. How many vacancies are available for IARI Young Professional-II recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There is 1 vacancy available for the Young Professional-II post.

faq.question: Q4. What is the educational qualification required for the Young Professional-II post?
faq.answer: Candidates must hold a Post Graduate Degree (M. Sc.) in Plant Biochemistry, Plant Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, Plant Physiology, Environmental Science, or Bioinformatics.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit for IARI Young Professional-II?
faq.answer: The upper age limit is 35 years as on the date of the interview, with age relaxation of 3 years for OBC and 5 years for SC/ST/women candidates as per government guidelines.

faq.question: Q6. What is the consolidated salary for this position?
faq.answer: The selected candidate will receive a consolidated fellowship of Rs 42,000/- per month.

faq.question: Q7. What documents must candidates bring to the interview?
faq.answer: Candidates must bring two copies of the application in the Annexure 1 format, a biodata with duly attested certificates from 10th standard onwards, an affixed recent passport size photograph, and an NOC from the current employer if working.

faq.question: Q8. Is this IARI Young Professional-II job permanent?
faq.answer: No, the position is purely temporary and contractual, co-terminus with the project (currently approved up to 31 March 2027), and does not offer a claim for regular appointment.

faq.question: Q9. Who gets age relaxation and how much is it?
faq.answer: An age relaxation of 3 years is given to OBC candidates and 5 years to SC, ST, and women candidates as per government guidelines.

faq.question: Q10. Are desirable qualifications mandatory for attending the interview?
faq.answer: No, desirable qualifications such as experience in basic molecular techniques, biochemical techniques, Omics data characterization, or gene cloning are preferred, but essential qualifications are mandatory to be entertained for the interview.
